name: DP83848IVVX_NOPB
title: 10/100 Mb/s Ethernet PHY (PHYTER), one port, MII/RMII/SNI, 48-pin QFP
summary: The DP83848 is a one-port 10BASE-T / 100BASE-TX Ethernet PHY on a 3.3 V supply, with integrated filters, adaptive equalization and baseline wander correction for 100BASE-TX, auto-negotiation with parallel detection, and Auto-MDIX. It talks to the MAC over MII, RMII or 10 Mb SNI, is managed over MDC/MDIO, drives three status LEDs and gives out a 25 or 50 MHz clock. Four grades share the die: C (0 to 70 °C) and I (-40 to 85 °C) in a 48-pin LQFP, VYB (-40 to 105 °C) and YB (-40 to 125 °C) in a 48-pin HLQFP with exposed pad; JTAG is on all but the C.
key_figures: 25 MHz crystal or oscillator; 50 MHz oscillator in RMII

notes: The temperature grade in the part number: C commercial, I industrial, VYB extended, YB extreme. X before /NOPB marks tape and reel.

pins.name: TX_CLK
pins.function: Transmit clock to the MAC. MII: 25 MHz at 100 Mb/s, 2.5 MHz at 10 Mb/s, taken from the 25 MHz reference. SNI: 10 MHz; the MAC launches TX_EN and TXD_0 on it. Not used in RMII, where X1 (50 MHz) times both directions.

pins.name: TX_EN
pins.function: Transmit enable, active high: TXD[3:0] (MII), TXD[1:0] (RMII) or TXD_0 (SNI) carry valid data while it is high.

pins.name: TXD_0
pins.function: Transmit data bit 0. Used in MII (TXD[3:0] on TX_CLK), RMII (TXD[1:0] on the 50 MHz reference) and SNI (the single serial data line, on the 10 MHz TX_CLK).

pins.name: TXD_1
pins.function: Transmit data bit 1 (MII and RMII).

pins.name: TXD_2
pins.function: Transmit data bit 2 (MII).

pins.name: TXD_3/SNI_MODE
pins.function: Transmit data bit 3 (MII). At reset it is sampled as the SNI_MODE strap: with MII_MODE high it chooses RMII (0) or 10 Mb SNI (1).

pins.name: PWR_DOWN/INT
pins.function: Power-down input by default: pull low to power the device down (same as BMCR bit 11). With MICR INT_OE set it becomes an open-drain, active-low interrupt output; an external pull-up may be needed besides the weak internal one.

pins.name: TCK
pins.function: JTAG test clock, weak internal pull-up. No JTAG on the DP83848C: leave pins 8 to 12 open.

pins.name: TDO
pins.function: JTAG test data output (not on the DP83848C).

pins.name: TMS
pins.function: JTAG test mode select, weak internal pull-up (not on the DP83848C).

pins.name: TRST#
pins.function: JTAG test reset, asynchronous and active low, weak internal pull-up (not on the DP83848C).

pins.name: TDI
pins.function: JTAG test data input, weak internal pull-up (not on the DP83848C).

pins.name: RD-
pins.function: Receive pair, negative side. Accepts 100BASE-TX or 10BASE-T automatically; with Auto-MDIX it may become the transmit pair. Needs a 3.3 V bias.

pins.name: RD+
pins.function: Receive pair, positive side (see RD-).

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground.

pins.name: TD-
pins.function: Transmit pair, negative side, a common driver set automatically for 10BASE-T or 100BASE-TX; with Auto-MDIX it may become the receive pair. Needs a 3.3 V bias.

pins.name: TD+
pins.function: Transmit pair, positive side (see TD-).

pins.name: PFBIN1
pins.function: Power feedback input: fed only from PFBOUT, with 0.1 µF placed close to the pin.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground.

pins.name: RESERVED
pins.function: Reserved: pull up to AVDD33 through 2.2 kΩ.

pins.name: RESERVED
pins.function: Reserved: pull up to AVDD33 through 2.2 kΩ.

pins.name: AVDD33
pins.function: Analog 3.3 V supply.

pins.name: PFBOUT
pins.function: Power feedback output. Place 10 µF (tantalum preferred) and 0.1 µF in parallel close to it, and wire it to PFBIN1 and PFBIN2.

pins.name: RBIAS
pins.function: Bias resistor: 4.87 kΩ, 1 % to ground.

pins.name: CLK_OUT
pins.function: Reference clock output for other devices on the board: 25 MHz in MII mode, 50 MHz in RMII mode.

pins.name: LED_ACT/COL/AN_EN
pins.function: LED output: activity in mode 1, collision in mode 2, collision or full duplex in mode 3. Sampled at reset as the AN_EN strap (high: auto-negotiation on).

pins.name: LED_SPEED/AN1
pins.function: LED output, on at 100 Mb/s and off at 10 Mb/s in every LED mode. Sampled at reset as the AN1 strap.

pins.name: LED_LINK/AN0
pins.function: LED output: on with good link (mode 1); on with link and blinking with activity (modes 2 and 3). Sampled at reset as the AN0 strap.

pins.name: RESET_N
pins.function: Active-low reset. A low of 1 µs or more resets the device: all registers go to their defaults and every strap is sampled again.

pins.name: MDIO
pins.function: Management data, bidirectional, driven by the station or the PHY. Needs a 1.5 kΩ pull-up.

pins.name: MDC
pins.function: Management data clock for MDIO, independent of the data clocks. 25 MHz maximum, no minimum.

pins.name: IOVDD33
pins.function: I/O 3.3 V supply.

pins.name: X2
pins.function: Crystal output, to a 25 MHz crystal. Leave open when X1 is driven by a CMOS oscillator.

pins.name: X1
pins.function: Reference clock input: a 25 MHz crystal across X1 and X2 or a 25 MHz CMOS oscillator on X1 alone, ±50 ppm. In RMII mode a 50 MHz, ±50 ppm CMOS oscillator is required.

pins.name: IOGND
pins.function: I/O ground.

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Digital ground.

pins.name: PFBIN2
pins.function: Power feedback input: fed only from PFBOUT, with 0.1 µF placed close to the pin.

pins.name: RX_CLK
pins.function: Receive clock recovered from the line. MII: 25 MHz at 100 Mb/s, 2.5 MHz at 10 Mb/s. SNI: 10 MHz. Not used in RMII.

pins.name: RX_DV/MII_MODE
pins.function: Receive data valid, high while RXD carries valid data (MII). In RMII it flags valid receive data apart from carrier sense; not used in SNI. Sampled at reset as the MII_MODE strap (internal pull-down, so MII by default).

pins.name: CRS/CRS_DV/LED_CFG
pins.function: Carrier sense, high while the medium is not idle (MII and SNI; in SNI it frames RXD_0). In RMII it is CRS_DV, carrier sense and receive data valid combined. Sampled at reset as the LED_CFG strap (mode 1 by default).

pins.name: RX_ER/MDIX_EN
pins.function: Receive error, high when an invalid symbol arrives at 100 Mb/s (in RMII, while CRS_DV is high); a MAC may ignore it since the PHY corrupts the data on an error. Not used in SNI. Sampled at reset as the MDIX_EN strap: a pull-down turns Auto-MDIX off.

pins.name: COL/PHYAD0
pins.function: Collision detect, high while transmit and receive are active together in half duplex; also a pulse of about 1 µs after each 10BASE-T half-duplex transmission when heartbeat is on; always low in full duplex. Not needed in RMII. Sampled at reset as PHYAD0 (internal pull-up).

pins.name: RXD_0/PHYAD1
pins.function: Receive data bit 0. MII: RXD[3:0] on RX_CLK, valid while RX_DV is high. RMII: RXD[1:0] on the 50 MHz X1 clock. SNI: the single serial receive line, valid while CRS is high. Sampled at reset as PHYAD1 (internal pull-down).

pins.name: RXD_1/PHYAD2
pins.function: Receive data bit 1 (MII, RMII). Sampled at reset as PHYAD2 (internal pull-down).

pins.name: RXD_2/PHYAD3
pins.function: Receive data bit 2 (MII). Sampled at reset as PHYAD3 (internal pull-down).

pins.name: RXD_3/PHYAD4
pins.function: Receive data bit 3 (MII). Sampled at reset as PHYAD4 (internal pull-down).

pins.name: IOGND
pins.function: I/O ground.

pins.name: IOVDD33
pins.function: I/O 3.3 V supply.

pins.name: GNDPAD
pins.function: Exposed ground pad.

notes: Types: I input, O output, I/O both, OD open drain, PU/PD internal pull-up/pull-down, S strap pin sampled at reset.
Each strap pin has a weak internal pull-up or pull-down. To strap the other level use an external 2.2 kΩ resistor; never tie a strap pin straight to VCC or GND, since most become outputs after reset.
The DP83848C has no JTAG; pins 8 to 12 stay unconnected on it.

circuits.title: 10/100 Mb/s twisted pair interface
circuits.description: Each line pair is terminated at the PHY by two 49.9 Ω resistors in series, their midpoint tied to Vdd and decoupled by 0.1 µF; the RD and TD pins require a 3.3 V bias. Each pair then runs through a 1:1 transformer whose PHY-side centre tap is also on Vdd with its own 0.1 µF to ground, and the far windings go to the RJ45. Resistor values are ±1 %. The termination parts sit close to the PHY and the centre-tap capacitors close to the transformer; common-mode chokes may be needed.

notes: T1 pins: RX_P1, RX_CT, RX_P2 are the PHY-side winding of the receive transformer (RX_P1 dotted), RX_S1 and RX_S2 its line side (RX_S1 dotted); TX_ pins likewise for the transmit transformer.

circuits.title: 25 MHz crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 25 MHz parallel-resonant AT-cut crystal across X1 and X2, with a load capacitor from each end to ground and an optional series resistor between X2 and the crystal to limit drive. With the crystal's needs unknown, start from 33 pF for CL1 and CL2 and 0 Ω for R1; the crystal vendor's load values take precedence.

parts.note: parallel resonant, AT cut, 20 pF load

circuits.title: Power feedback connection
circuits.description: PFBOUT feeds the two PFBIN inputs. PFBOUT carries 10 µF, tantalum preferred, in parallel with 0.1 µF, and each PFBIN pin has its own 0.1 µF, all to ground and each placed at its pin. Nothing else may power the PFBIN pins.

circuits.title: Auto-negotiation straps with LEDs
circuits.description: Each LED pin is pulled to VCC by 2.2 kΩ, which straps AN_EN, AN1 and AN0 to 1: auto-negotiation on, advertising 10 and 100 Mb/s in half and full duplex. Because the straps sampled high, the LED outputs drive active low, so each LED runs from VCC through 110 Ω with its cathode on the pin.

circuits.title: PHY address strap
circuits.description: A 2.2 kΩ pull-up to VCC on RXD_0 sets PHYAD1; COL keeps its internal pull-up (PHYAD0 = 1) and RXD_1 to RXD_3 their internal pull-downs, so the PHY answers at address 00011 (03h). After reset the five pins are the MII receive outputs COL and RXD_0 to RXD_3.

operation.text: One design in four temperature grades: DP83848C 0 to 70 °C, DP83848I -40 to 85 °C, DP83848VYB -40 to 105 °C, DP83848YB -40 to 125 °C. C and I come in the 48-pin LQFP (PT), VYB and YB in the 48-pin HLQFP with exposed pad (PTB); all are 7 mm × 7 mm bodies. The DP83848C lacks JTAG.

A 10/100 Mb/s transceiver for twisted pair, typically under 270 mW from 3.3 V. The extended-range device is qualified to AEC-Q100 Grade 2. It works with a 25 MHz clock in MII mode and needs a 50 MHz clock in RMII mode; MII or RMII is chosen by strap or register.

An internal power-on reset means no external reset is needed after power-up. A hardware reset is a TTL low of at least 1 µs on RESET_N; a software reset is BMCR bit 15 and takes about 1 µs. Both reload every register default and sample the straps again; wait 3 µs after a software reset before further MDIO traffic. After power-up the X1 clock must run stably for 167 ms before straps are latched and MDIO access starts (84 ms in RMII mode).

PHY address, auto-negotiation mode, MAC interface mode, LED mode and Auto-MDIX are read from pins at reset; most of those pins then become outputs. Each has a weak internal pull resistor giving its default. To change one, use a 2.2 kΩ pull resistor, never a direct tie to VCC or GND, and keep the RC time short enough that the level settles before the pin turns into an output.

PHYAD0 is on COL and PHYAD1 to PHYAD4 on RXD_0 to RXD_3, latched into PHYCR[4:0] at power-up and hardware reset. COL pulls up and the RXD pins pull down, so the default address is 00001 (01h). Every PHY on one MDIO bus needs its own address. Strapping address 0 puts the part in MII isolate mode; writing 0 into PHYCR does not.

Entered by BMCR bit 10 or by strapping address 0. The PHY ignores TXD[3:0] and TX_EN and floats its MII outputs (CRS, COL, RXD[3:0], RX_ER, RX_DV, RX_CLK and TX_CLK), but still answers management. The line side keeps sending 100BASE-TX scrambled idles or 10BASE-T link pulses, and auto-negotiation or parallel detection can still bring a link up.

Exchanges abilities with the link partner in fast link pulse bursts (IEEE 802.3 Clause 28) and picks the best common mode, in the order 100BASE-TX full, 100BASE-TX half, 10BASE-T full, 10BASE-T half. AN_EN, AN1 and AN0 set the power-up behaviour and ANAR bits 8:5; BMCR (00h) can change it at any time. With auto-negotiation off, BMCR speed and duplex bits set the mode. PHYSTS (10h) reports the result once link is up. ANLPAR becomes 0081h or 0021h after parallel detection to 100 or 10 Mb/s.

With a partner that does not auto-negotiate, both receivers watch for valid 100BASE-TX or 10BASE-T link signals and the matching mode is chosen. ANLPAR bit 7 or 5 then marks the partner's mode and bits 4:0 read 00001; a 0 in the partner auto-negotiation-able bit with negotiation complete shows the link came by parallel detection. Anything other than a single good link sets the parallel detect fault bit. Parallel detection cannot see duplex, so a partner forced to full duplex ends up in half duplex.

BMCR bit 9 restarts negotiation, and losing a negotiated link restarts it too. On a restart the PHY stops all transmit and link pulses until the break_link_timer (about 1500 ms) runs out, so the partner sees link fail, then sends FLP bursts again. If the part came up forced and negotiation is wanted from software, clear and then set BMCR bit 12. Auto-negotiation or parallel detection takes about 2 to 3 s, also with next pages depending on how many are sent.

On by default; set by the MDIX_EN strap or PHYCR bits 15:14. It uses auto-negotiation to find the right pair assignment and swaps pairs from a random seed, per IEEE 802.3. It does not work in a forced mode. A crossover can be forced with PHYCR bit 14 (FORCE_MDIX) without auto-negotiation or Auto-MDIX.

Three LED outputs: LED_LINK, LED_SPEED and LED_ACT/COL, in three modes chosen by the LED_CFG strap or PHYCR bits 6:5 (mode 3 by register only). A 100BASE-TX link comes from signal detect on a compliant input; a 10 Mb/s link from seven consecutive normal link pulses or a valid packet; link drops on the IEEE 802.3 link loss timer. In 10 Mb/s half duplex the collision LED follows COL. Each LED pin shares a strap, and its drive polarity follows the strapped level: a pin pulled low drives active high, a pin pulled high drives active low. LEDCR (18h) can drive the LEDs directly; it cannot read them.

BMCR bit 14 sends MII transmit data back to the MII receive outputs without putting it on the line; PHYSTS bit 3 shows it. Turn auto-negotiation off before entering loopback. At 100 Mb/s loopback starts with up to 550 µs with no receive data while the descrambler locks.

A built-in self test sends a PSR9 or PSR15 pseudo-random stream (PHYCR PSR_15) and checks it on return, through internal loopback or an external loop cable. PHYCR BIST_STATUS starts at 0 (fail), sets on good compares and latches on a miscompare until the start/stop bit is written. CDCTRL1 bit 5 gives continuous transmission for VOD tests, and CDCTRL1 bits 15:8 count errors.
With energy detect on (EDCR, 1Dh) and no cable activity the device sits in low power, still watching the line and now and then sending energy detect pulses; activity starts a normal power-up.

The IEEE 802.3 Clause 22 nibble interface: RXD[3:0], RX_ER, RX_DV and RX_CLK on receive; TXD[3:0], TX_EN and TX_CLK on transmit, both clocks 2.5 MHz at 10 Mb/s and 25 MHz at 100 Mb/s; plus CRS and COL. The management interface runs in every MAC interface mode.

In half duplex a collision is transmit and receive active at once, flagged on COL for as long as it lasts. While transmitting at 10 Mb/s a collision is reported only after seven bits in the collision state, to reject noise; during receive it is reported at once. With heartbeat on, about 1 µs after each 10 Mb/s packet an SQE pulse of about 10 bit times appears on COL. CRS rises on receive activity (squelch passed at 10 Mb/s; valid signal detect plus two non-contiguous zeros at 100 Mb/s), and in half duplex also on transmit; it falls after end of packet. In full duplex collision detection is off and CRS shows receive only.

RMII rev 1.2 uses TX_EN, TXD[1:0], RX_ER (optional for the MAC), CRS_DV, RXD[1:0] and a 50 MHz clock on X1 for both directions; an extra RX_DV is also given. RMII needs a 50 MHz oscillator; a 50 MHz crystal is not supported, and the mode must be set by strap. At 10 Mb/s data moves once every 10 clocks. A receive elasticity buffer, set in RBR[1:0] in 4-bit steps, absorbs the difference between the reference and recovered clocks; overrun or underrun forces a frame check error and is reported in RBR.

MDC (25 MHz max, no minimum) and MDIO give access to thirty-two 16-bit registers; up to 32 devices may share MDIO. MDIO needs a 1.5 kΩ pull-up, which holds it high in idle and turnaround. After power-up or reset, and after a bad start, opcode or turnaround, the PHY waits for 32 ones on MDIO (driven, or left to the pull-up while 32 MDC cycles run) before answering. Start is 01; in a read the PHY releases the first turnaround bit, drives 0 in the second and then the data; in a write the station sends 10 as turnaround.
BMSR bit 6 reads 1: after the single 32-bit preamble that follows a reset, frames may go without preamble, with at least one idle bit between them.
A 10 Mb/s serial (7-wire) interface for 10 Mb-only controllers: TXD_0, TX_EN and TX_CLK to transmit, RXD_0, RX_CLK, CRS and COL to receive, clocked at 10 MHz with separate transmit and receive paths.

Half and full duplex at both speeds. Half duplex follows CSMA/CD and CRS reports transmit and receive. In full duplex, giving up to 200 Mb/s per port at 100BASE-TX, collision sensing is off and CRS reports receive only. All other MII signalling is the same in both.

Turns MII nibbles into a 125 Mb/s scrambled MLT-3 stream: 4B5B encoding (J/K replaces the first preamble byte, T/R ends the frame, idles fill the gaps), scrambling, NRZ to NRZI and binary to MLT-3 in a common driver that goes straight to the magnetics. The scrambler is an 11-bit closed-loop LFSR seeded from PHYAD[4:1], cutting emissions at some frequencies by up to 20 dB. The MLT-3 output is slew limited; the magnetics must keep the transition time between 3 and 5 ns. Binary output at 100 Mb/s is not possible.

An analog front end with equalization and gain control, then a DSP with adaptive equalization, gain control and baseline wander compensation, then signal detect, MLT-3 and NRZI decoding, serial to parallel, descrambling, code group alignment on J/K, 4B5B decoding, a link integrity monitor and bad SSD detection. The equalizer adapts to cable length and type (attenuation curve). Baseline wander correction recovers the TP-PMD killer pattern, an event of about 800 mV offset for 120 ms. 10BASE-T link pulses and FLP bursts do not raise signal detect.

The descrambler locks after 12 consecutive idle code groups. A hold timer of 722 µs restarts each time enough idles (58 bit times) arrive; if not, the descrambler resets and relocks. Signal detect must hold for 395 µs before the link monitor goes to link up and enables transmit and receive.
A change from idles to non-idles without a leading J/K raises RX_ER and puts 1110 on RXD[3:0] until at least two idles arrive, then RX_ER and CRS drop; FCSCR counts one.

An IEEE 802.3 transceiver covering jabber, link integrity, heartbeat, collision and loopback besides transmit and receive, and the transmit and receive filters built in: only the isolation transformers and termination resistors are needed, and transmit harmonics are at least 30 dB down. Half duplex is CSMA/CD; full duplex transmits and receives at once without collisions.

Valid data needs a pulse past the squelch level of one polarity, then past the opposite level within 150 ns, then past the first again within 150 ns; this typically costs three preamble bits. Data is valid until no squelch-level pulse is seen for over 150 ns (end of packet); once data is found the squelch levels are lowered.

Link pulses are about 100 ns wide every 16 ms when idle; without valid link pulses the 10BASE-T transmitter, receiver and collision detection shut off, unless FORCE_LINK_10 is set. Jabber cuts the transmitter after about 85 ms of continuous transmission and restores it after transmit enable has been low for about 500 ms. Three inverted link pulses in a row flag reversed polarity in 10BTSCR, and the receiver corrects it internally. SQE is off in full duplex or with HEARTBEAT_DIS set.

The encoder starts when TX_EN rises and sends pre-emphasized Manchester data, TXD valid at the TX_CLK rising edge; the last transition is always positive, mid-cell for a final one and at the cell end for a final zero. The decoder sees end of frame when mid-bit transitions stop, drops carrier sense within 1.5 bit times and keeps RX_CLK running for five more bit times.

Pin 7 is a power-down input by default and an active-low interrupt output when MICR bit 0 (INT_OE) is set. Driving it low equals BMCR bit 11; an external pull-down makes the device start powered down, and setting INT_OE over MDIO then releases it. Interrupts: set MICR bit 1 (INTEN), choose sources in the low byte of MISR, read the high byte to see which fired; one read clears all. For link change or energy detect: write 0003h to MICR, 0060h to MISR, then watch the pin.

A 25 MHz crystal across X1 and X2, or a CMOS oscillator on X1 with X2 open: 25 MHz in MII mode, 50 MHz in RMII mode, ±50 ppm. The crystal is parallel resonant, AT cut, 20 pF load. The oscillator drives it at 100 µW minimum and 500 µW maximum (misprint: a 100 mW minimum should read 100 µW). A crystal rated for lower drive takes a series resistor between X2 and the crystal.
PFBOUT carries 10 µF (tantalum preferred) plus 0.1 µF close to pin 23, and connects to PFBIN1 (pin 18) and PFBIN2 (pin 37), each with 0.1 µF at the pin. The PFBIN pins take power only from PFBOUT.
RBIAS takes 4.87 kΩ 1 % to ground. Reserved pins 20 and 21 each pull up to AVDD33 through 2.2 kΩ.

Use an isolation transformer with an integrated common-mode choke, or an RJ45 with the magnetics built in, meeting the magnetics requirements table. Run no signals under the magnetics, and void the planes under discrete magnetics.

The MAC may be a separate chip or inside a processor or FPGA. MII lines are 68 Ω per IEEE. Fit 50 Ω series resistors on all MII outputs, RX_CLK, TX_CLK and receive data included. Keep MII and RMII traces under 6 inches and matched within 2.0 inches, with controlled impedance and no stubs.

Put the 49.9 Ω 1 % resistors and their 0.1 µF next to the TD± and RD± pins, with a via straight to the Vdd plane. MDI traces are 50 Ω to ground, 100 Ω differential; each pair runs side by side, matched in length, on one layer if possible, with no stubs, few vias and no crossing of a plane split. Use at least four layers, with the high speed signal layers next to ground or Vdd planes; with an isolated chassis ground plane, a signal layer can sit between chassis ground planes, or between Vdd planes inside chassis ground planes.

Bypass each Vdd pin with a low-impedance 0.1 µF surface-mount capacitor as close as possible, between the pin and its via to the plane. A 0 Ω resistor in series with a supply pin leaves room for a ferrite bead if EMI testing needs one. Add 10 µF near the PHY for bulk, and give the board a solid Vdd plane and a solid ground plane, at least one of each.
Built-in ESD protection is limited; store and handle the parts with leads shorted or in conductive foam.
